mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in demand (GDPC1) signals stronger economic activity, compressing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days are not significantly positive when GDPC1 increases, despite no other contradictory indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate below 2.5% signals accommodative monetary policy, lowering borrowing costs and stimulating equity investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns over 5 days are not positive despite FEDFUNDS falling below 2.5%, indicating the policy did not translate into expected market gains.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of falling federal funds rates (easing) and decreasing unemployment rates (strong labor market) creates a synergistic effect, driving up investor confidence and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction of FEDFUNDS falling and UNRATE falling does not lead to significantly positive returns, suggesting the combined signal is not predictive in this context.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a surge in demand (GDPC1 exceeding 19,000) accelerates economic momentum, reducing risk premiums and elevating S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns over 60 days remain non-positive despite GDPC1 crossing above 19,000 in a late-cycle expansion, indicating the signal did not materialize as expected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising labor demand (PAYEMS increasing) reflects stronger job market conditions, boosting corporate profits and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns over 5 days are negative despite increasing labor demand, suggesting external factors outweighed the labor signal.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in both demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) indices signals robust economic expansion, reducing uncertainty and driving up S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The simultaneous rise in GDPC1 and INDPRO does not correlate with significantly positive S&P 500 returns, indicating the combined signal lacks predictive power.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in unemployment rates below 3% strengthens labor market confidence, attracting investment and lifting S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns over 5 days remain negative despite UNRATE falling below 3%, suggesting the labor signal did not translate into market gains.

mechanism_narrative: In a recession recovery phase, a surge in supply indices above 110 reflects improving business conditions, reducing deflationary pressures and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns over 60 days are not positive despite INDPRO exceeding 110 in a recession recovery, indicating the signal did not materialize as expected.
